data.name: Stitched HD
data.detailed_description:
Stitched is a horror adventure game that strings together the thrilling story of Catherine Stockholmes, an otherwise ordinary girl. The story begins with Catherine waking up in an eerie doll factory. With a great desire to escape, Catherine is forced to venture through the factory. But little does she know that terrible fates always befall the curious ones. Will Catherine muster enough courage to needle her way out of the factory? Or will she fall into sheer despair and perish?




Catherine Stockholmes: An 18 year old girl with a sweet and honest personality. She was diagnosed with a serious heart condition at a young age. Her symptom will worsen whenever she is frightened. This can potentially lead to her passing out or worse, death.



Doll: A mysterious doll that displays a calm and stoic expression. She seems to know more about the incident that occurred in the doll factory than she lets on.



Boy: A strange but simple boy who is constantly searching for his missing parents. He seems to be seeking for more than just his parents...




Compelling story:
- Drives gameplay and exploration.

Unsettling atmosphere:
- Feel the suspense of not knowing what lies behind each door.

Meticulously detailed, hand drawn cut scenes:
- Original art brings scenes to life.

Thoroughly developed characters:
- Make decisions based on character actions and motives.

Heart-stopping chase sequences:
- Tread carefully.

A variety of engaging puzzles:
- Solve puzzles in order to progress as well as unlock secrets.

data.short_description: A pleasantly anticipated trip back home for the holidays becomes a nightmare for Catherine as a tragic accident leaves her unconscious. After coming to her senses, she realizes that something is dreadfully wrong. She must escape the doll factory she awoke in before it's too late.

reviews.review:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
The title I shall review today is one of the best RPG Maker projects that I’ve played and written about on Steam so far. I’m not exaggerating one bit. In fact, it makes me feel even more conflicted since I cannot share any screenshots of the game with you, for the annoying reason that the Steam Overlay is not supported by it. And Stitched fully deserves to be showcased through its clever puzzles and talented artwork which screams “labour of love”. An exceptional Steam debut for developer Fluffex Studios and I am going to partially overlook the aforementioned flaw that never hindered my in-game progress or interfered with the overall experience. For a game that’s spent 3 years in development, there aren’t many flaws to complain about anyway.

[h1]Story[/h1]
As with any good RPG, whether it’s rendered in 3D or not, the storyline is paramount. Stitched is obviously featuring an original story which borrows very few elements from pre-existing works of Horror fiction. As for similar video games I could compare its narrative threads to, the closest contender would be the “American McGee's Alice” series. Yet Stitched is more likely a tale about our inner fears and coping with them, than a battle with our inner demons or madness. We have a young female protagonist and her name is Catherine Stockholmes. She’s a college student and suffers from a rare heart condition. A car crash injures her further more to the point of induced coma. It is at this point that I’m able to draw more connections to McGee’s own twisted vision for Alice in Wonderland. Granted that Lewis Carroll’s original novel bares little resemblance to any form of logic, perhaps Catherine’s brutal adventure is only a convincing nightmare that she’s experiencing as part of the trauma she’s sustained.

We can’t really tell but the smiling, carefree and beautiful girl that was on her way home from college, is far too quickly replaced by a terrorised shell of her former self, easily startled, bearing scars (physically and mentally) along with the titular stitches that now cover most of her body. It leaves a powerful impression for certain. I like the contrast created between her preference for vivid colors and the gloomy corridors featuring the occasional pool of blood or gore. A reminder of the ongoing struggle for closure and escape, no doubt. Catherine’s purple dress is the “drop of color”, feeling out of place in this entire macabre spectacle of uncertainty. I shall not spoil the game’s plot or subplots. Suffice to say, our heroine finds herself prisoner inside the Stockholmes Research Institute. A fancy name for her father’s toy factory which seems to focus on mechanical dolls. If you’re as much into symbolism as I am, then you’ll rejoice since this title features plenty of interpretable elements, objects and events.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
My trusty sources at ModDB (most contemporary video game have detailed pages over there with technical specs) confirm that Stitched is powered by RPG Maker VX Ace, same as another horror 2D RPG I reviewed a while back, Story of the Survivor. It’s a pleasant break from Unity or Unreal and in theory, I could work my way through that engine as well since Humble Bundle offered a killer deal for it a few months ago. In practice, I currently lack any game development skills so I’ll stick to writing for the time being. My point is, RPG Maker VX Ace can showcase some very nice visual assets if you have some great ideas that need to be brought to digital life. Stitched is such a case and the only thing truly preventing me from enjoying it to its full potential, is the complete absence of Steam Overlay support. I didn’t mind that I can’t see the frame rate, but preventing me from taking screenshots and linking them to my Steam profile? That is a cardinal sin in my books yet I decided that I won’t lower the final rating too much since I firmly believe that this design oversight can get fixed eventually.

Even without being able to have screenshots to remind me of my time spent in Stitched, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the artwork which can be admired from the game’s main menu, once unlocked through story progression. Sprite animations are also top notch and prove that you don’t always need 3D rendering, in order to convey any convincing horror elements. The options menu is light on customization, yet its fullscreen mode was decent enough. You can switch to windowed mode by pressing F5, but there’s really no reason to do that unless you’re multitasking. My only advice in this case, is that you focus on this game and its captivating story. You can save the progress often enough via statues that are present in nearly all of the game’s levels. And with good reason since even slight mistakes can lead to “Game Over”. Play it safe and patiently examine your surroundings.

[h1]Audio[/h1]
Some limited form of voice acting is present, since the heroine always has something to say and a text-only option wouldn’t have sufficed. The soundtrack and general effects are also adequately represented which means that I cannot complain at all about what I’ve heard so far in Stitched. It’s not like I expected ringtone-like cheery (and simplistic) tunes like in most indie JRPGs. No self-respecting title claiming to belong to the Horror genre can divert from well established eerie sounds.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Miss Stockholmes must constantly evade murderous animatronics, yet you’ll never feel like playing another Five Nights at Freddy's  since we’re dealing with a more subtle kind of horror which never relies on cheap jump scares. Hiding from dolls and a monstrous bear, Catherine must also struggle with an elusive enemy that can be just as deadly. Her own damaged psyche. A fright level is the game’s defining gameplay mechanic and you may have already seen this type of challenge in the Amnesia series or the even older (and a true classic) Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth. Long story short, you step on or look too much at disturbing imagery and your body begins to slip, initially towards catatonia and ultimately leading to cardiac arrest. Catherine’s weak heart can’t handle too much gore and even stepping in pools of blood seems to unsettle her more than you’d expect from a “scream queen”. That’s where Stability Pills come into play. I don’t know if they’re a derogatory term for Diazepam, but those drugs do seem to keep Catherine focused enough for her mission.

Two more Pill types are available, yet their usefulness is limited. One for extra movement speed and another for briefly highlighting points of interest on the level map. Addictive or not, it’s better to use them sporadically and simply avoid any disturbing objects that are clearly covered in blood. I kinda wished that the protagonist might be able to fight back at least sometimes instead of just hiding. She must face her fears afterall, if she desires to find an escape from this waking nightmare. I kept the best part of Stitched for my closing arguments in its favor. Puzzle sections that really goona make your brain squirm. Never too challenging, yet far more developed than what I’ve seen for this genre in a very long time. An almost old school type of difficulty that doesn’t hold your hand by offering too many clues or successful alternatives. You want that key, since you can’t progress without it? Then you better solve that chromatic or mathematical/logical puzzle since there’s no other way out of this issue.

[h1]Verdict, Summary & Rating are below in the Comment Section.[/h1]
